shopify.title: Connect Shopify
shopify.intro: Two ways: a custom app created in the store admin (fastest, one store) or a public app with OAuth (one install flow for every customer).

steps.title: Create the custom app
steps.body: In the store admin open Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop apps → Create an app. Name it “Hullwise”.

steps.title: Grant Admin API scopes
steps.body: In Configuration → Admin API integration select the scopes listed on the right for the modules the customer bought. Save.

steps.title: Install and copy the token
steps.body: Install the app, then reveal the Admin API access token once (shpat_…) and the API secret key. Paste both in Hullwise → Integrations → Shopify → Connect. Hullwise stores them encrypted (AES-GCM).

steps.title: Webhooks
steps.body: Hullwise registers its webhook subscriptions through the API at connect time against {webhookUrl}. For a custom app the signing secret is the app's API secret key. The endpoint answers 200 within milliseconds, stores the event and processes it in the background; duplicates are ignored by (topic, id, updated_at).

steps.title: Initial import
steps.body: Click Resync: locations, products, inventory and discounts are imported, then orders page by page with a resumable cursor. Large stores continue across several worker runs; progress is visible under “Recent sync runs”.

steps.title: Products: what Hullwise edits
steps.body: Hullwise mirrors every product field on read (media, description, status and channels, organisation, variants, SEO, metafields) and writes back only title, description, vendor, type, tags, status, SEO, category, variant price, compare-at price, SKU, barcode, weight, inventory policy and media (add from URL, reorder, remove, alt text). Scopes: read_products and write_products; read_publications to show the sales channels. Everything else opens the product in the Shopify admin. An edit opened before a change made in Shopify is refused with “changed in Shopify, reload”.

steps.title: Order state rules
steps.body: Hullwise never derives the order status from fixed tags. Open Settings → Order states and map the store's tags, payment methods and financial/fulfillment statuses to the canonical states; preview the result on the last 50 orders.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Test connection shows the shop name and the granted scopes; place a test order in the store and watch it appear in Orders within seconds, with an “imported” event in its timeline.

steps.title: Public app (optional)
steps.body: Create the app in the Partner dashboard, set the redirect URL to /api/integrations/shopify/oauth/callback, put the client id and secret in SHOPIFY_API_KEY and SHOPIFY_API_SECRET, then use “Install via OAuth”.

errors.fix: The token was revoked or copied incompletely. Create a new token in the app and reconnect.
A scope is missing: the card shows which. Add it in the app configuration and reinstall.
The signing secret differs from the one saved in Hullwise. Reconnect with the current API secret key.
Normal under heavy sync: Hullwise waits and retries automatically; the run resumes from its cursor.

meta.title: Connect Meta Ads
meta.intro: Hullwise reads campaigns, ad sets, ads and asset breakdowns with daily insights, and can pause or resume campaigns and ads with an explicit confirmation. A system user token keeps the connection alive without personal logins.

steps.title: Create a system user
steps.body: In Business Settings → Users → System users create an Admin system user named “Hullwise”.

steps.title: Assign the ad account
steps.body: Add assets → Ad accounts → select the account → Manage campaigns (needed for pause/resume) or View performance (read-only).

steps.title: Generate the token
steps.body: Generate new token → choose the app → permissions ads_read and business_management, plus ads_management only to pause from Hullwise → never expires. Copy it once.

steps.title: URL parameters
Asset breakdowns
steps.body: Headline, text, image and video breakdowns exist only for dynamic creative and Advantage+ creative ads; other ads show no assets.

steps.title: Connect in Hullwise
steps.body: Integrations → Meta Ads → Connect: paste the ad account id (act_…) and the token. Test connection shows the account name and granted permissions.

steps.title: Backfill
steps.body: Resync pulls the last 30 days in 7-day windows for campaigns, ad sets, ads and assets; the nightly job refreshes the last 3 days because Meta restates recent insights.

errors.fix: Token expired or revoked: generate a new one for the system user.
Rate limit on the ad account: Hullwise pauses the backfill and resumes it later from the same window.
The system user lacks the ad account asset or the permission; fix it in Business Settings.

meta.scopes: Reading: ads_read and business_management. Optional, only to pause campaigns and ads from Hullwise: ads_management.

google.title: Connect Google Ads
google.intro: Read-only by default: campaigns, ad groups, ads, responsive ad assets, keywords and search terms with daily cost, clicks and conversions. Pausing ads and negative keywords need write access, granted by the store.

steps.title: Developer token
steps.body: From a Manager (MCC) account open Tools → API Center and request a developer token; Basic access is enough for production reads.

steps.title: OAuth client
steps.body: In Google Cloud create an OAuth client (Web or Desktop) with the Google Ads API enabled; note client id and secret.

steps.title: Refresh token
steps.body: Authorise the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords with a user who can access the customer account and keep the refresh token. Use a user with standard (edit) access only if the store wants Hullwise to pause ads and add negative keywords.

steps.title: API version
steps.body: Hullwise calls the Google Ads API {apiVersion}. Google retires each version about a year after release: check the sunset dates page and plan the update before that date.

steps.title: Tracking template
Connect in Hullwise
steps.body: Integrations → Google Ads → Connect: customer id (digits), manager id when accessed through an MCC, developer token, client id/secret, refresh token.

steps.title: Write access (optional)
steps.body: If the store wants negative keywords and ad pauses from Hullwise, tick “Write access granted” on the Google Ads card. Every write asks for confirmation and goes through the write queue.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Test connection runs a one-row GAQL query; Resync imports campaigns, then ad groups, ads, assets, keywords and search terms in 7-day windows (resumable, rate limits respected).

errors.fix: The developer token is not approved for this account, or the login-customer-id is missing for an MCC-managed account.
The refresh token was revoked; authorise again and reconnect.
The API version was retired: Hullwise needs an update of the version constant.

errors.symptom: Hullwise orders show a dash on keywords
errors.fix: The tracking template is missing or lacks utm_term with the keyword parameter.

google.scopes: Reading: the adwords scope with read access and a Basic developer token. Optional, only to pause ads and add negative keywords: the same scope with a user who can edit the account.

anthropic.title: Connect the AI assistant (Anthropic)
anthropic.intro: The assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key: Anthropic bills the usage to your account, and Hullwise only stores the key, encrypted. Without a key the Assistant page asks to connect one.
anthropic.scopes:
No permission scopes: one API key from the store's own Anthropic account.
What is sent to the model: the question, and the figures of the reports the assistant reads to answer (totals, product and campaign names; for customer predictions, customer names and amounts). The assistant can never change data.

steps.title: Create the Anthropic account
steps.body: Go to console.anthropic.com and sign up with a company email. Create the organization in the store's name, so the invoices go to the store.

steps.title: Add credits and a spend limit
steps.body: Settings → Billing: add a payment method and buy credits. Settings → Limits: set a monthly spend limit, so the cost can never surprise you.

steps.title: Optional: a workspace for Hullwise
steps.body: Settings → Workspaces → Create workspace "Hullwise". Usage then shows separately in the console, and the workspace can have its own spend limit.

steps.title: Create the API key
steps.body: Settings → API keys → Create key, in the Hullwise workspace if you made one, named "Hullwise". Copy it now: the console shows it only once.

steps.title: Paste it in Hullwise
steps.body: Integrations → AI (Anthropic) → Connect, paste the key, Connect. Hullwise checks the key by reading the model's details (no tokens spent) and stores it encrypted. "Test connection" repeats the check at any time.

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: Open Assistant and click a suggested question. Under each answer you see the figures with their period and a link to the report. The side panel shows this month's tokens; the same usage appears in the Anthropic console → Usage.

steps.title: Who can use it
steps.body: Every role can ask questions. The assistant only reads the reports the user's role can open, and each user's conversations are private.

errors.fix: The key was copied incompletely, revoked, or belongs to a disabled workspace. Create a new key and connect again.
New Anthropic accounts start with low rate limits, which rise with usage and credits purchased. Wait a minute; if it happens daily, check the limits in the console.

errors.symptom: "Credit balance is too low" in the console, answers failing
errors.fix: Add credits in Settings → Billing, or turn on auto-reload.
Start a new conversation. If it repeats, the model may not be available on the account: check the console.

tracking.title: Activate the pixel and server-side conversions
tracking.intro: The pixel runs on the store; conversions use the Meta and Google connections already in Integrations. No extra credentials are stored for the pixel.
tracking.scopes:
Meta: the system user token needs the dataset (pixel) assigned with Manage access.
Google: a conversion action of type "Import → clicks", and Customer data terms accepted for user identifiers.
Privacy: decide which consent category (marketing or analytics) the pixel runs under.

steps.title: Copy the custom pixel
steps.body: Integrations → Pixel & conversions → copy the Shopify custom pixel. It already contains this store's collect address.

steps.title: Add it in Shopify
steps.body: Shopify admin → Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel → name it "Hullwise" → paste the code → Save → Connect.

steps.title: Set the customer privacy permission
steps.body: In the pixel's settings choose the permission that matches your consent policy (Marketing or Analytics). With Shopify's cookie banner the pixel only runs after consent.

steps.title: Check that events arrive
steps.body: Browse the store in a private window, then reload the Pixel & conversions page: events and sessions grow, and an order placed from that window shows its journey. "Send test event" checks Hullwise's side alone.

steps.title: Meta: dataset and token access
steps.body: Events Manager → Data sources → your dataset (pixel) → copy its id. In Business Settings → System users → Hullwise → Add assets → Datasets, give it Manage access. Optional: copy a Test event code from Events Manager → Test events to see the first events there.

steps.title: Avoid double counting with Meta
steps.body: If Shopify's Facebook & Instagram app already sends Conversions API events ("Maximum" data sharing), keep only one server source: either turn that off or leave Hullwise's Meta sending disabled.

steps.title: Google: conversion action
steps.body: Google Ads → Goals → Conversions → New → Import → Other data sources or CRMs → Track conversions from clicks; category Purchase. Copy the conversion action id (ctId in the address bar). Accept the Customer data terms under Goals → Settings to send hashed identifiers.

steps.title: Enable and run
steps.body: Enter the ids, keep "Only customers who accept marketing" unless your legal basis says otherwise, save, then Run queue now. The delivery log shows each order's outcome; the job repeats every 5 minutes.

errors.fix: The custom pixel is not connected, consent was not given in the test browser, or the store origin is not in the allowed list.
The token expired or the system user lost the dataset: generate a new token or reassign the dataset.
The dataset id is wrong, or the event is older than 7 days.
Wrong id, or the action belongs to another account (check the manager account in the Google connection).
Expected when consent is required and customers have not opted in to marketing.

survey.title: Activate the post-purchase survey
survey.intro: A one-question survey ("How did you hear about us?") linked from the order confirmation email. Answers feed the survey-blend attribution model and the Survey tab in Analytics.
survey.scopes: No platform permission: the link is built by the email template with the store's survey secret (Analytics → Survey).

steps.title: Turn the survey on
steps.body: Analytics → Survey → Survey active, adjust the question and option labels in each language, save.

steps.title: Copy the email link
steps.body: The same tab shows the link with this store's secret. It signs the order id with Shopify's hmac_sha256 filter.

steps.title: Add it to the order confirmation
steps.body: Shopify admin → Settings → Notifications → Order confirmation → Edit code. Paste the link where you want the question to appear (after the order summary works well) and save. Send a test email to yourself.

steps.title: Optional: thank-you page
steps.body: A survey block on the thank-you page needs a Shopify checkout UI extension (an app). Until then the email link is the supported path.

steps.title: Read the results
steps.body: Answers appear in Analytics → Survey within seconds. Choose the "Survey blend" model in Attribution to give answered orders' credit partly to the channel customers named.

errors.fix: The template changed the order id (use order.id, not order.name) or the secret was copied incompletely.
The survey is not active.
Move the link higher in the email; one question with big options answers in a second.

email.title: Platform email (Resend)
email.intro: Hullwise sends sign-in links, invitations, notifications and digests from one platform sender. This guide is for the platform administrator: tenants need nothing.

steps.title: Create the Resend account
steps.body: Sign up at resend.com with the platform administrator mailbox and turn on two-factor authentication.

steps.title: Add the sending domain
steps.body: Domains → Add domain. Use a subdomain dedicated to transactional mail (for example mail.yourdomain.com) and the region closest to your users.

steps.title: SPF
steps.body: Add the MX and TXT records Resend shows for the bounce subdomain (the TXT is an SPF record such as v=spf1 include:… ~all). Keep a single SPF record per name.

steps.title: DKIM
steps.body: Add the DKIM TXT record (resend._domainkey.…) exactly as shown, then wait until Resend marks the domain Verified.

steps.title: DMARC
steps.body: Publish a TXT record on _dmarc.yourdomain.com, for example v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com. Move to p=quarantine once the reports are clean.

steps.title: Sending-only API key
steps.body: API Keys → Create API key with permission “Sending access”, restricted to the verified domain. It is shown once and starts with re_.

steps.title: Set the Railway variables
steps.body: On the web and worker services set RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM (e.g. Hullwise <no-reply@mail.yourdomain.com>, on the verified domain), EMAIL_REPLY_TO (the support mailbox) and HULLWISE_INTEGRATION_MODE=live; optionally EMAIL_LEGAL_NAME, EMAIL_LEGAL_ADDRESS and EMAIL_SUPPORT_ADDRESS for the footer. Redeploy. Never commit the key.

steps.title: Delivery webhook
steps.body: Webhooks → Add endpoint {emailWebhookUrl} with the events email.delivered, email.delivery_delayed, email.bounced and email.complained. Copy the signing secret (whsec_…) into RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET on the web service.

steps.title: Send a test email
steps.body: Console → Email must read “Resend is sending”. Send a test email to a mailbox you control, open the original message and check that SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass. The log shows the email as delivered once the webhook arrives.

email.scopes: One API key with “Sending access” only, restricted to the sending domain. Never a full-access key.

errors.fix: RESEND_API_KEY is missing on the service or HULLWISE_INTEGRATION_MODE is not live: set both and redeploy.
EMAIL_FROM uses a domain Resend has not verified yet: finish the DNS records or use a verified domain.
The key was revoked or has no sending access: create a new sending-only key.
Resend limits requests per second and per day: the queue retries with backoff; upgrade the plan if it persists.
RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is missing or differs from the endpoint signing secret: the webhook answers 401 or 503.

tiktok.title: Connect TikTok Ads
tiktok.intro: Campaigns, ad groups and ads (copy, video, thumbnail) with daily spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, conversion value and video views, from every authorized advertiser account. Pausing and resuming campaigns and ads asks for confirmation and goes through the write queue. Included from the Growth plan.

steps.title: Create the TikTok for Business app
steps.body:
On the TikTok API for Business developer portal create an app (or use Hullwise’s, when TIKTOK_APP_ID is configured). Set the advertiser redirect URL to:
{callbackUrl}

steps.title: Permissions
steps.body: Request the permission groups the activated modules need (panel on the right): Ad Account Management, Ads Management and Reporting for campaigns and metrics; Creative Management for video thumbnails. TikTok reviews the app before it can be used on accounts other than yours.

steps.title: Authorize the advertiser accounts
steps.body: The store owner (or an admin of its Business Center) opens the authorization link, picks the advertiser accounts and confirms. TikTok redirects back with an auth_code valid for a few minutes and usable once.

steps.title: Connect in Hullwise
steps.body: Integrations → TikTok Ads → Connect: app id, app secret and the auth code (or “Authorize with TikTok” with Hullwise’s app). Hullwise exchanges the code for a long-lived access token, stores it encrypted (AES-GCM) and imports every advertiser it covers.

steps.title: UTM template
API version
steps.body: Hullwise calls the TikTok API for Business {apiVersion} (reporting: report/integrated/get, daily rows in windows of up to 30 days). Check the changelog before each release.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Test connection reads the advertiser accounts; Resync imports campaigns and daily metrics, then ad groups and ads in 7-day windows (resumable, rate limits respected). The first import covers the last 90 days.

errors.fix: The advertiser revoked the authorization or the token was rotated: authorize again and reconnect.
The app lacks a permission group, or the advertiser account was not selected during the authorization.
Rate limit: Hullwise pauses the sync and resumes from the same window after the wait.
The auth code lasts a few minutes and works once: run the authorization again.
The URL parameters miss utm_content=__CID__ / utm_term=__AID__, or the store drops ttclid from the landing URL.

tiktok.scopes: Read-only analysis needs Ad Account Management and Reporting; pause/resume needs Ads Management too. Without Creative Management everything works except thumbnails.

modules.campaigns: Campaigns, ad groups, ads and metrics

subscriptions.title: Connect your subscription app
subscriptions.intro: Subscriptions are read from the app that bills them: Shopify Subscriptions, Recharge or Loop. Contracts, renewal charges and cancellations are imported; pauses, skips, swaps and cancellations made by your team go back through the app. Cards are never charged here and selling plans are edited in the app.
subscriptions.scopes: Shopify Subscriptions: the contract scopes are "own" scopes, so an app reads only the contracts it created; contracts created by the Shopify Subscriptions app need Shopify's approval for third-party access. Recharge and Loop: an API token with the permissions listed above.

steps.title: Choose the app the store uses
steps.body: Check where subscriptions are sold today (Apps in the Shopify admin). One subscription app per store: connecting another replaces it.

steps.title: Shopify Subscriptions: add the contract scopes
steps.body: In the custom app of the Shopify connection (Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop apps → your app → Configuration), add read_own_subscription_contracts, write_own_subscription_contracts and read_customer_payment_methods, save and reinstall the app so the token gets them.

steps.title: Shopify Subscriptions: contracts of the Shopify app
steps.body: Contracts created by the Shopify Subscriptions app belong to that app. Ask Shopify Support (or check the Partner dashboard) for access to subscription contracts of other apps before going live; without it the sync sees no contracts.

steps.title: Recharge: create the API token
steps.body: Recharge → Apps & integrations → API tokens → Create an API token with read and write access to subscriptions, charges and customers, and read access to orders. Copy the token and the API client secret.

steps.title: Loop: create the API token
steps.body: Loop admin → Settings → API access → Create token with subscriptions read/write, orders and customers read. Copy the token and the webhook signing secret.

steps.title: Connect in Subscriptions or Integrations
steps.body: Integrations → Subscription app → Connect: choose the app; for Recharge and Loop paste the token and the secret (stored encrypted). Shopify Subscriptions reuses the Shopify connection.

steps.title: Register the webhooks
steps.body: In the app's webhook settings, point the topics listed on the right to {subscriptionsWebhookUrl}. Events are verified with the signing secret and imported once; the sync every 15 minutes catches anything missed.

steps.title: Check that it works
steps.body: Press Test connection, then Resync: subscribers, MRR and charges appear in Subscriptions. Try a pause on a test subscription and check that the app shows it paused.

errors.fix: Add the scopes to the Shopify custom app and reinstall it, then test again.
The contracts belong to another app: request access to other apps' contracts from Shopify, or connect the app that bills them (Recharge, Loop).
The token was revoked or rotated: create a new one in the app and connect again.
The app throttled the requests: the sync pauses and resumes from where it stopped at the next run.
The app does not support it (Recharge has no pause, for example): use the app's own admin.

integration_guide.ad_hoc_notice: Ad hoc integration: {product} already has the interface and a simulated provider, so every screen works in the demo. The live connector for the store's provider is built and switched on by the {product} team for this account (it is quoted separately). The store only provides the account and the credentials listed below.

address.title: Address validation (Google)
address.intro: Checks shipping addresses and suggests complete ones while the team edits an order; the COD add-on uses the same check in the delivery score. {product} uses the store's own Google Maps Platform key: Google bills the requests to the store's Google Cloud account. Without a key {product} keeps a format check (required fields, postal code pattern per country).
address.scopes:
No OAuth scopes: one API key from the store's Google Cloud project, with two APIs enabled. Restrict the key to these two APIs.
What is sent to Google: the address lines, city, postal code, province and country of the address being checked or the text typed in the search box. Never the customer's name, email or phone.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: Order page → Edit → shipping address: while typing, up to 3 suggestions with the full structured address; on save, the address is validated and problems are shown per field (missing house number, postal code that does not match the city, street not found). The team can still save after reading the warning. With the COD add-on the address quality factor of the delivery score uses the same answer.

steps.title: Create or choose a Google Cloud project
steps.body: console.cloud.google.com → project picker → New project, named after the store (e.g. "Store – {product}"). Use the store's own Google account so the invoices go to the store.

steps.title: Turn on billing
steps.body: Billing → Link a billing account to the project. Google Maps Platform needs billing even within the monthly free usage. Set a budget alert (Billing → Budgets & alerts), for example at the expected monthly cost.

steps.title: Enable the two APIs
steps.body: APIs & Services → Library: enable "Address Validation API" and "Places API (New)". The old "Places API" is not the same product: {product} calls Places API (New).

steps.title: Create and restrict the API key
steps.body: APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → API key. Then Edit API key → API restrictions → Restrict key → select Address Validation API and Places API (New). Application restrictions: "None" ({product} calls Google from its servers, not from a browser); do not use HTTP referrer restrictions, they block server calls.

steps.title: Paste the key in {product}
steps.body: Integrations → Address validation → Connect, paste the key (it starts with AIza), Connect. {product} validates one known address to check the key and the APIs, then stores the key encrypted. Owners and admins only.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Open an order → Edit → shipping address, type a street of your city: suggestions appear in a second. Change the postal code to a wrong one and save: the dialog shows the postal code warning. "Test connection" on the card repeats the check at any time.

steps.title: Costs to expect
steps.body: Each validation is one Address Validation request; each search shows up to 3 suggestions = one Autocomplete request plus one Place Details request per suggestion. Check the current prices and the monthly free usage on the Google Maps Platform pricing page before going live.

errors.symptom: Test connection: "Google rejected the API key"
errors.fix: The key was copied incompletely, deleted or restricted to other APIs. Check API restrictions on the key, or create a new one.

errors.symptom: "API is not enabled on the Google Cloud project"
errors.fix: Enable Address Validation API and Places API (New) in the same project as the key; it can take a few minutes to apply.
Link a billing account to the project (Billing → Link a billing account).
Places API (New) is not enabled or not allowed by the key's API restrictions.

errors.symptom: The edit dialog shows only format warnings
errors.fix: Google did not answer (quota, outage): {product} falls back to the format check so the team is never blocked. Look at the quotas page in Google Cloud and at the card's last error.

payment_guarantee.title: Card hold for instant exchanges
payment_guarantee.intro: With instant exchange on (Returns → Policy and automations), the replacement ships as soon as the return is approved. To cover the risk, {product} places a hold on the customer's card for the value of the items still to come back: it is released when they arrive and captured if they do not arrive within the configured days. Today the hold is simulated; the live hold runs on the store's payment provider.
payment_guarantee.scopes:
Stripe (manual capture): a restricted key with write access to PaymentIntents and read access to Customers and PaymentMethods; webhook events payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated, payment_intent.canceled, payment_intent.succeeded.
Shopify Payments: the vaulted card can be charged only through Shopify's own flows; check with the {product} team which ones apply to the store's plan before selling it.
In every case the customer's consent to the hold must be part of the return portal text.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: On an approved instant exchange {product} asks the provider to authorise the value of the returned items, shows the hold on the return (authorised, released, captured), releases it when the goods are received and captures it from the returns job after the configured days, flagging the return for review. A failed hold ships nothing early and flags the return.

steps.title: What the store needs
steps.body: A payment provider that supports holds on a saved card: typically Stripe with manual capture (cards authorised at checkout or saved for later use). Holds expire on the card network's terms (often 7 days for online card payments): the instant exchange window must not be longer than what the provider allows.

steps.title: Create the credentials
steps.body: Stripe dashboard → Developers → API keys → Create restricted key, named "{product} holds", with the permissions listed on the right. Copy it once; Stripe shows it only at creation.

steps.title: Send them to the {product} team
steps.body: Send the key through the secure channel agreed with the {product} team (never by plain email). {product} stores it encrypted (AES-GCM) in the integration and connects the store's account; the store does not paste anything in {product}.

steps.title: Policy and portal text
steps.body: Returns → Policy and automations → Instant exchange: set the days within which the goods must come back. Returns → Portal: add to the confirmation text that the store will place a temporary hold of the items' value on the card.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: With the {product} team, run one instant exchange on a test order in the provider's test mode: the return shows "hold authorised", the provider shows an uncaptured payment of the same amount; mark the return received and the hold is released.

errors.fix: The card declined the authorisation or needs the customer's confirmation (3-D Secure). The replacement is not shipped early; contact the customer or approve a normal exchange.

errors.symptom: Hold captured although the goods arrived
errors.fix: The return was marked received after the capture date. Refund the captured amount from the provider and shorten the receiving time, or lengthen the instant exchange days.

errors.symptom: Hold expired before the goods arrived
errors.fix: The card network released it before the configured days: lower the instant exchange days to what the provider allows.

return_labels.title: Prepaid return labels
return_labels.intro: Gives the customer a prepaid label (or a QR code for drop-off) when the return is submitted from the portal. Today {product} issues a simulated label and prints the PDF itself; the live connector asks the store's carrier or label service for a real one and stores the tracking code on the return.
return_labels.scopes:
Shipping label aggregators (EasyPost, Shippo and similar): an API key of the store's account, with return labels enabled and a payment method on file.
A carrier's own API: the store's customer number, API credentials and the return product enabled on the contract ("return label" / "pay on use").
{product} needs: the return destination address (Returns → Portal → Prepaid return label) and the parcel's default weight.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: Returns → Portal → "Give the customer a prepaid return label". When a return is submitted, {product} asks the provider for a label from the customer's address to the destination you set, stores carrier and tracking code on the return, shows the label link on the confirmation page and in the approval email, and uses the tracking code to follow the parcel back.

steps.title: What the store needs
steps.body: A contract with a carrier that offers return labels, or an account with a label aggregator, with return labels paid on use if possible (you pay only for labels actually scanned).

steps.title: Create the credentials
steps.body: In the provider's dashboard create a production API key (and a test key) for {product}. With a carrier API, ask the account manager to enable return labels on the customer number.

steps.title: Send them to the {product} team
steps.body: Send the keys and, for a carrier, the customer number through the secure channel agreed with the {product} team. {product} stores them encrypted and activates the connector on the store's account.

steps.title: Set the destination
steps.body: Returns → Portal: enable the prepaid label and write the destination address (one line per row). The label cost per return (Returns → Portal → Refunds and the store) feeds the P/L.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Submit a test return from the portal (/r/<store>): the confirmation shows "Download the label" and the return shows carrier and tracking code. In the provider's dashboard the label appears under the test key.

errors.symptom: No label on the confirmation page
errors.fix: The prepaid label is off in the portal settings or the destination address is empty.

errors.symptom: The provider refuses the customer's address
errors.fix: The address is incomplete or in a country the return product does not cover; the return is created anyway and the team can send instructions by email.
Choose "pay on use" return labels where the provider offers them.

audiences.title: Segments to ad audiences
audiences.intro: Sends a CRM segment to Meta as a Custom Audience, to Google Ads as a Customer Match list, or to an email tool as a list, and keeps it in step: customers who enter the segment are added, those who leave are removed. Today the destinations are simulated; the live connectors use the store's own ad accounts.
audiences.scopes:
Meta Custom Audiences: a system user token with ads_management on the ad account, and the Custom Audience terms accepted on that ad account.
Google Customer Match: the Google Ads connection's OAuth scope (https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords) on an account that meets Google's Customer Match policy (account history and spend), customer data terms accepted.
Email tool: an API key allowed to manage lists or audiences.
Only customers with marketing consent are sent; ad platforms receive only SHA-256 hashes of normalized email and phone.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: Segments → a segment → Live updates and destinations → Add destination: choose Meta, Google or the email tool. {product} creates the audience the first time, then syncs differences after every change of the segment (or on request), with status and readable error per destination.

steps.title: Meta: accept the terms
steps.body: Business Settings → the ad account → Custom Audiences terms, or Ads Manager → Audiences → Create audience → Custom audience → Customer list, and accept the terms once.

steps.title: Meta: give the token the permission
steps.body: Business Settings → Users → System users → the {product} system user → Assign assets → the ad account with "Manage campaigns" (ads_management). The same token used for Meta Ads can be reused.

steps.title: Google: check eligibility
steps.body: Google Ads → Tools → Shared library → Audience manager → Your data segments: if Customer Match is available, the account is eligible. Accept the customer data terms when asked.

steps.title: Email tool
steps.body: Create an API key that can manage lists (audiences, contacts) and note the list or audience id if one already exists.

steps.title: Send them to the {product} team
steps.body: Meta and Google reuse the connections already in Integrations once the {product} team activates the destination; the email tool key goes through the secure channel agreed with the {product} team and is stored encrypted.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Push a small segment: after the sync the destination shows the number sent; in Meta Audiences or Google's Audience manager the list appears with "populating" and the match rate after a few hours.

errors.fix: Accept the Custom Audience terms on the same ad account the token uses.
The account does not meet Google's policy yet (history, spend, compliance); ask Google support or use another account.
Ad platforms need a minimum number of matched people: widen the segment or wait for it to grow.
Only customers with marketing consent and an email or phone are sent.

messaging.title: Messaging channels (email, SMS, WhatsApp)
messaging.intro: The channel that sends CRM campaigns to segments (customer campaigns add-on) and, where the store wants it, order messages. {product} has the interface and a simulated channel that records every message; the live connector for the store's provider is built by the {product} team. Status emails about returns do not need this: they go through {product}'s platform sender.
messaging.scopes:
Email marketing provider: an API key allowed to send (and manage lists, if campaigns use its lists), a verified sending domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC).
SMS provider: an API key, a registered sender id or number, and the country registrations the provider requires.
WhatsApp Business: an account with a WhatsApp Business Solution Provider or the Cloud API, a verified business, a phone number, and approved message templates for each campaign message.
Webhook for delivery status: {product} gives the URL to paste in the provider when it activates the connector.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: With the customer campaigns add-on: a campaign picks a segment, a channel and a template, sends to the treated group and keeps the control group out, then measures the difference. Each message has a status (sent, delivered, read, failed) from the provider's webhook.

steps.title: Choose the provider
steps.body: Use the provider the store already pays for if possible: the {product} team builds one connector per provider. Tell the team the provider name and the channels you want (email, SMS, WhatsApp).

steps.title: Prepare the account
steps.body: Email: verify the sending domain. SMS: register the sender id. WhatsApp: verify the business in Meta Business Manager, connect the number and get the message templates approved (marketing templates need opt-in).

steps.title: Create the credentials
steps.body: Create an API key dedicated to {product} in the provider's dashboard, with send permission only where possible.

steps.title: Send them to the {product} team
steps.body: Send the key, the sender (domain, sender id or number) and the template names through the secure channel agreed with the {product} team. {product} stores them encrypted and registers the delivery webhook.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: With the {product} team, send a test campaign to a segment with only your own contact: the message arrives, and the campaign shows it as delivered (and read for WhatsApp).

errors.fix: The template is not approved, or the customer did not opt in for marketing messages.

errors.symptom: SMS not delivered in a country
errors.fix: The sender id is not registered there; check the provider's country rules.
Complete SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the sending domain and warm it up with small volumes.
The provider's delivery webhook is not configured or points to an old URL.

carrier.title: Carrier tracking and delivery instructions
carrier.intro: A second source for the shipment status, next to Shopify's fulfilment events: the carrier's own tracking events (in transit, out for delivery, failed attempt, exception) and the channel to send delivery instructions for a parcel in exception (redeliver, new address, pickup point, return). Today the carrier is simulated; in live mode, until a connector is active, instructions go by email to the carrier address set in Settings → Fulfilment.
carrier.scopes:
Carrier API: the store's customer number and API credentials with tracking access (and, for instructions, the parcel management / delivery change service enabled on the contract).
Tracking aggregator: an API key of the store's account that covers the carriers the store uses.
{product} needs: the list of carriers and services the store ships with.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: Shipments: each parcel's status is resolved from every source with precedences (the carrier's event wins over an older Shopify state). Exceptions and stuck parcels open work items; from a parcel in exception the team sends an instruction to the carrier, and the answer is logged on the order timeline.

steps.title: What the store needs
steps.body: API access on the carrier contract: many carriers give it on request to business customers, sometimes as a paid option. With several carriers, a tracking aggregator covers all of them with one key.

steps.title: Create the credentials
steps.body: Ask the carrier's account manager for API credentials for tracking (and delivery instructions), or create the key in the aggregator's dashboard.

steps.title: Send them to the {product} team
steps.body: Send the credentials and the customer number through the secure channel agreed with the {product} team. {product} stores them encrypted and activates the connector; meanwhile, instructions from Fulfilment → Exceptions go by email.

steps.title: Status mappings
steps.body: Settings → Fulfilment → status mappings: check how the carrier's statuses map to {product}'s (in transit, exception, delivered). The {product} team pre-fills them for the carrier.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Open a recent parcel: the timeline shows events with source = carrier. Send an instruction on a test parcel in exception: the order timeline shows "Delivery instruction sent" with the carrier's reference.

errors.fix: The tracking numbers from Shopify are for another carrier or service than the one connected; check the carrier name on the fulfilments.
The parcel is already delivered or returned, or the delivery change service is not on the contract.
Two sources disagree: review the status mappings in Settings → Fulfilment.

warehouse.title: Warehouse / 3PL
warehouse.intro: Connects an external logistics provider: {product} sends it the orders to ship, reads its stock and the shipment status it reports. Today the warehouse is simulated; the live connector for the store's 3PL is built by the {product} team.
warehouse.scopes:
3PL API: credentials of the store's account with permission to create outbound orders, read stock per SKU and read shipment status; the warehouse code(s) to use.
SKUs must match between Shopify and the 3PL: {product} matches stock and order lines by SKU.
If the 3PL already connects to Shopify directly, decide with the {product} team which system sends the orders, so they are not sent twice.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: Orders ready to ship are pushed to the 3PL; its stock per SKU updates the location's inventory in {product} (a dedicated location); its shipment status becomes a source of the shipment resolver. Stock differences show up in Inventory.

steps.title: What the store needs
steps.body: A 3PL with an API, and the SKU on every Shopify variant matching the 3PL's article code.

steps.title: Create the credentials
steps.body: Ask the 3PL for API credentials for {product} (test and production) and the warehouse code.

steps.title: Send them to the {product} team
steps.body: Send the credentials and the warehouse code through the secure channel agreed with the {product} team. {product} stores them encrypted, creates the 3PL location and activates the connector.

steps.title: Check the SKUs
steps.body: Products → Catalog data quality → "Missing SKU": every variant shipped by the 3PL needs one; duplicates are refused.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: With the {product} team: an order created in the test store reaches the 3PL's test environment; a stock change at the 3PL appears in Inventory for the 3PL location after the next sync.

errors.fix: A line has no SKU, or the SKU is unknown at the 3PL.
The 3PL counts reserved units differently; compare with Inventory and agree which figure {product} shows.
Both Shopify's own 3PL app and {product} send orders: keep only one sender.

spoki.title: WhatsApp with Spoki
spoki.intro: Connects the store's Spoki account (a WhatsApp Business Solution Provider): COD confirmations and replies, order notifications, WhatsApp campaigns and opt-outs, with every message on the order and customer pages.
spoki.scopes:
A Spoki account with a verified WhatsApp Business number and an API key (Settings → Developers).
Approved WhatsApp templates for every event you want to send outside the 24-hour window (utility for order messages, marketing for campaigns).
The webhook URL of this page in Spoki's webhook settings, for message status, replies and opt-outs.

steps.title: What it does in {product}
steps.body: COD add-on: the confirmation message goes through Spoki and a reply such as “yes” confirms the order in the queue (a “no” escalates it to an admin). Order notifications: confirmed, shipped and delivered, each with its own template and switch. Customer campaigns: WhatsApp campaigns are sent through Spoki. A “STOP” reply puts the number on the shared suppression list.

steps.title: Create the API key
steps.body: In Spoki: Settings → Developers (or Integrations → API) → create an API key for {product}.

steps.title: Connect it in {product}
steps.body: Integrations → WhatsApp (Spoki) → Connect → paste the key. {product} tests it by reading the templates and stores it encrypted.

steps.title: Paste the webhook URL in Spoki
Get the templates approved
steps.body: In Spoki create the templates (one per event, with custom fields such as FIRST_NAME or ORDER_NAME) and submit them to WhatsApp. Approval usually takes minutes to a day.

steps.title: Map the templates
steps.body: Integrations → WhatsApp (Spoki) → Resync reads the approved templates. In WhatsApp settings choose a template per event, map its custom fields to {product}'s variables and switch on the notifications you want.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Send a COD confirmation from an order to your own number: the message log shows Sent, then Delivered and Read as Spoki reports them. Reply “yes”: the order is confirmed in the queue.

errors.fix: The number is not on WhatsApp or cannot receive messages; check the phone on the order.
The customer stopped marketing messages: {product} adds the number to the suppression list.
Top up the Spoki account; sends fail until then.
Outside 24 hours from the customer's last message WhatsApp accepts only approved templates: map one to the event.
The webhook URL is missing or wrong in Spoki; copy it again from the integration card.

settings.description: Operators and their hours, scoring weights and thresholds, recipient risk. Nothing here acts automatically on orders: the add-on advises, operators decide.
settings.operators_description: Orders are distributed in proportion to the hours worked today (smooth weighted round-robin). Days off and extra hours override the weekly plan.
settings.weights_description: Relative weights 0–50. A factor with weight 0 is shown but ignored. The score is the weighted mean of the factors that fire, then capped by the recipient risk tier.
settings.risk_description: Returns weighted by age (recent 1.0, older 0.5); one tier of redemption after consecutive deliveries.
settings.recipients_description: Suggestions only: nothing is blocked automatically. Keys are phones or emails, never names.
settings.suggest_blacklist: Suggest blacklist: verify by phone before shipping
settings.suggest_verify: Verify address and intent before shipping
settings.tags_description: How the queue talks to your store through order tags. Nothing is hard-coded: an empty list means that tag flow is not used. Matching ignores case; a trailing * matches a prefix (vendita* matches "Vendita Marco").

tags_read_help.queue: An order carrying one of these enters (or returns to) the queue, whatever its status. Shown on the row and usable to route operators.
tags_read_help.confirmed: Closes the queue item and confirms the order when the tag appears on the platform.
tags_read_help.cancelled: Closes the queue item as cancelled. Precedence: cancelled, then confirmed, then queue.

settings.tags_write_help: Platform first, then Hullwise: if the store rejects the write, nothing is recorded. Tags already present are not added twice.
settings.tags_clear_on_close: On confirmed and cancelled also remove every queue tag

steps.title: Open the connectors
steps.body: In Claude (web or desktop app) open Settings → Connectors and choose “Add custom connector”. On team plans an owner may have to allow custom connectors first.

steps.title: Paste the server URL
Sign in and approve
steps.body: Claude opens Hullwise: sign in, pick the workspace, keep or remove the permissions and approve. You return to Claude connected.

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: In a chat, enable the connector from the tools menu and ask: “How did sales go last week compared with the week before?” Claude cites the figures with a link to Hullwise.

steps.title: Allow custom connectors
steps.body: In ChatGPT open Settings → Connectors (Apps). Depending on the plan, custom MCP connectors need developer mode under Advanced settings, or an admin of the workspace.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.body: Choose Create, give it a name, paste {serverUrl} and pick OAuth as the authentication.

steps.title: Sign in and approve
steps.body: ChatGPT opens Hullwise: sign in, pick the workspace and the permissions, approve.

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: Start a chat, add the connector from the tools menu and ask for example: “Which campaigns lost money this month and what does Hullwise suggest?”

steps.title: Open the MCP settings
steps.body: In Cursor open Settings → MCP (Tools & Integrations) → “Add custom MCP server”: it opens ~/.cursor/mcp.json.

steps.title: Add Hullwise
steps.body:
Add this server and save:
{ "mcpServers": { "hullwise": { "url": "{serverUrl}" } } }

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Cursor shows the server as needing login: click it, sign in to Hullwise and approve. Without OAuth, create a personal access token and add "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer kpat_…" } to the server entry.

steps.title: Try it
steps.body: In the agent chat ask: “List the products at risk of stock-out with their suggested reorder.”
